title: Aisle Thirteen
hook: My manager gave me one rule for the night shift: if the intercom ever pages you to aisle thirteen... don't go.
lines: I stock shelves overnight at a grocery store on the edge of town.
Twelve aisles. Humming lights. And nobody else... ever.
My manager gave me one rule on my first shift.
If the intercom ever pages you to aisle thirteen... don't go. Just clock out, and leave.
For two months, that intercom never made a sound.
Then, last night, at three a.m.... it crackled.
A soft voice. Almost kind. Cleanup... on aisle thirteen.
I looked down the row of signs. One through twelve. Like always.
But past the freezers, at the far back wall, a thirteenth sign was swinging... over a dark aisle I had never seen.
I didn't go. I clocked out, and ran for the doors.
Behind me, one by one, the aisle lights started going dark... coming closer.
I backed into the last lit aisle, right by the doors.
And the soft voice came back... Cleanup... on aisle one.
